question.leadin: Answer the following about the Gaza Strip.
question.text: In 1993, Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization signed a series of accords named for this city, the capital of Norway. The accords gave Palestinians the right to self-government in Gaza.
question.clue: Gardermoen airport is the main one serving this city, where the exploration ship Fram and the Kon-Tiki raft can both be visited at museums.

swap.text: The Aland [Oh-land]Islands, a Swedish-speaking archipelago forming an autonomous region of Finland, are found in this gulf, the northernmost arm of the Baltic Sea. This gulf separates Finland and Sweden.
swap.clue: To the west of Finland is this gulf and northernmost arm of the Baltic Sea. It contains the Aland Islands and serves to separate Finland and Sweden.

question.text: This Norwegian terrorist set off a car bomb in Oslo and carried out a mass shooting in Utoya, which he claimed to do in order to fight against the forces of Islam and multiculturalism.
question.clue: First, name this right-wing extremist who was also responsible for the Utoya massacre, in which he opened fire on a crowd, killing 69 and injuring 66 at an AUF summer camp.

swap.leadin: Sten Sture the Younger's dead body was burned at the stake during an event in this city.
swap.text: Name this city whose ruler Christian II led a "bloodbath" against heretics. Uppsala preceded this city as the capital of the Kingdom of Sweden.
swap.clue: This city is located where the Riddarfjarden bay of Lake Malaren meets the Saltsjon and west of a namesake archipelago in the Baltic.

question.text: Canute was born a king of this non-Swiss country whose flag is a white cross on a red field.
question.clue: During its occupation by the Nazis, this country's resistance movement saved nearly all of its Jews, and its king apocryphally wore a yellow star in solidarity.

swap.leadin: This monarch appointed the chancellor Axel Oxenstierna, who negotiated the Truce of Altmark with Poland on this monarch's behalf.
swap.text: Name this Swedish king whose victory over the forces of the Count of Tilly at the Battle of Breitenfeld preceded his death at the Battle of Lutzen.
swap.clue: At the Battle of Lech, also known as the "Battle of Rain," he commanded troops over the Count of Tilly.

question.text: Hayha helped this country inflict massive casualties on the Soviets during the Winter War. This country then signed the Moscow Peace Treaty, but resumed fighting with the USSR in the Continuation War.
question.clue: As a grand duchy, this country's capital was originally at Turku.

swap.leadin: This city is home to a center of higher education endowed in the 17th century by the monarchy, where Carl Linnaeus worked as he taught his new system of biological classification.
swap.text: Name this non-capital city on the Fyris river in Scandinavia. Its country's Archbishop can be found in this city's domkyrka, a redbrick cathedral with three steeples.

question.text: Before losing at Hastings, Harold had defeated and killed this king of Norway at the Battle of Stamford Bridge.
question.clue: This man married the daughter of Yaroslav the Wise, Elisiv of Kiev, on his return from Constantinople.

swap.text: Ruling from 1632 to 1654, this queen patronized Rene Descartes and eventually abdicated the throne to become a Catholic penitent in Rome.
swap.clue: This "Minerva of the North" who was tutored by Rene Descartes. Axel Oxienstierna served as an advisor to this monarch after the death of her father at the Battle of Lutzen.

question.leadin: Christer Pettersen was convicted but later acquitted of this man's murder.
question.text: Name this politician from the Social Democratic Party, a prime minister of Sweden who was killed in 1986 while walking home from the cinema with his wife.

swap.leadin: Cowards die many times before their deaths: so, too, celebrities.
swap.text: Reading his own obituary, in which he was described as the 'merchant of death', this man resolved to bequeath his wealth to the establishment of a series of prizes in various academic fields.
swap.clue: This man bought the Bofors ironworks in 1894, transforming it into a prominent manufacturer of cannons.

question.leadin: Cardinal Mazarin remarked that if all the ministers of Europe were on the same boat, this person would be at the helm.
question.text: Name this Swedish politician. He served as regent for Gustavus Adolphus in his absence and, after his death in battle, regent for his young daughter Christina.

swap.leadin: Margaret I facilitated this union by serving as regent to her great-nephew Erik of Pomerania during his minority.
swap.text: Name this Scandinavian union which united three countries under a single monarch until the early 16th century.
swap.clue: This polity was weakened by earlier rebellions led by Amund Bolt in one member and Engelbrekt in another, leading to the deposition of its monarch, Eric of Pomerania.

question.leadin: This ship was salvaged in 1961, over 300 years after sinking on its maiden voyage.
question.text: Name this ship, now housed at a namesake museum in Stockholm. This ship shares its name with the dynasty of its commissioner, who was advised by Axel Oxenstierna.
question.clue: A queen from this royal house abdicated after converting to Catholicism and housed Descartes in his final years.

swap.text: Among the other regents after Charles VIII's reign were two different men with this name. The "Elder" of the two secured the Swedish throne for Christian I of Denmark.

question.text: For Frederick I's rule and some years afterwards the riksdag was dominated by these two political parties, one of which assumed control of parliament in 1738 before giving way to the other in 1765.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about insane CIA Cold War plots that did not involve exploding cigars or acoustic kitties.
swap.text: This place was long thought to contain a lost hydrogen bomb after a secret mission crashed at Thule Air Base. Project Iceworm wanted to build launch sites under this territory of Denmark, which is the world's largest island.
swap.clue: Henrik Kauffman signed a 1941 treaty with the United States paving the way for the establishment of Thule Airbase on this island.

question.text: Historians like L. K. Barlow used the sudden demise of this settlement to compare climate resilience between the Norse and Thule natives. Bishop Ivar Barðarson recorded the desolation of its largest site, Sandnes, up to a century before the larger Eastern Settlement to its south.

swap.leadin: Sweden's age of greatness didn't end with the death of Gustavus Adolphus.
swap.text: After Gustavus died in battle, the throne passed to this woman, his daughter. She invited Rene Descartes to teach philosophy in Sweden.
swap.clue: Although historians are not sure whether the abdication was influenced by a clandestine love for Cardinal Decio Azzolino, we do know that this ruler received educateion from Jorge Stiernhelm.
